status.label: Design ready — needs approval
status.detail: The Keyboard Manager editor issue already has two user reports plus logs showing native dependency startup failure. The fallback and launch paths are concrete enough to design a fix without waiting on more upstream triage.

next_action.label: Approve the detailed design
next_action.reason: Repository files, implementation steps, and verification are specific enough to start the fork-side fix when desired.

design.root_cause: When the native Keyboard Manager wrapper DLL (or one of its native dependencies) is unavailable, the editor startup path does not honor its own read-only fallback. `SettingsManager` already catches `DllNotFoundException` and says the editor can run in standalone mode from JSON settings, but `MainPage` immediately creates `KeyboardMappingService` again, catches the failure, and returns before presenting a recovery UI. The module launcher only checks that `PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorUI.exe` started, so the user sees a brief process and then nothing useful.
evidence: Issue #49434 includes logs showing `Powertoys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll` (or one of its dependencies) could not be loaded, followed by `MainPage.xaml.cs` logging `Failed to initialize mapping service`.
A second user reported the same silent-exit symptom after seeing a missing Windows App Runtime prompt and installing Windows App SDK 2.3.1 manually.

`src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Settings/SettingsManager.cs` catches `DllNotFoundException` and explicitly documents a standalone/read-only fallback when the native service is unavailable.

`src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs` still constructs `new KeyboardMappingService()` in the page constructor and returns early on failure, which bypasses the JSON-backed fallback already loaded by `SettingsManager`.

`src/modules/keyboardmanager/dll/dllmain.cpp` launches `WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorUI.exe` and treats process creation as success, without surfacing dependency-health diagnostics if the child exits immediately.

affected_files.purpose: Owns the native-wrapper probe and the JSON-backed fallback settings model that should remain usable when the DLL load fails.
Contains the service-down InfoBar and command surface that should reflect native-unavailable read-only mode instead of a silent exit.
Creates `KeyboardMappingService`, loads mappings, and should gate edit/save flows when the native service is unavailable.
Adds focused regression coverage for native-unavailable startup and read-only fallback behavior.
Launches the WinUI editor process and should emit clearer diagnostics when startup dependencies are unhealthy.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The settings layer can already fall back to JSON when the native wrapper fails to load, but it only exposes a boolean and the UI startup path does not consume a richer failure reason.
implementation_steps.change: Promote native-service probing into a first-class startup status (for example `NativeServiceStartupState`) that records whether the wrapper is available, why it failed, and whether JSON-only fallback data was loaded successfully.
edge_cases: Distinguish “wrapper missing” from “settings JSON corrupt” so the UI can show the right banner and avoid overwriting good data.
Keep `LoadSettings()` resilient when both the native wrapper and the JSON file are unavailable.
Do not attempt to regenerate JSON settings from the native service when the wrapper probe already failed.
tests: Add `SettingsManagerFallbackTests` that simulate missing native DLL load and assert `StartupState` becomes JSON-fallback-only instead of throwing.
Add a test that corrupt JSON still returns an empty settings model without crashing the editor.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The page contains a service-down InfoBar, but the constructor exits before the banner is configured when the native wrapper cannot be loaded, and the add/edit surface remains designed for fully writable mode.
implementation_steps.change: Bind the banner text and command enablement to the new startup state so the page opens in explicit read-only mode, disables add/edit entry points, and tells the user which dependency is missing plus how to recover.
implementation_steps.code_block:
<InfoBar
    x:Name="ServiceDownBanner"
    IsOpen="{x:Bind IsNativeFallbackMode, Mode=OneWay}"
    Message="Keyboard Manager started in read-only mode because the native editor dependencies are unavailable." />

<Button x:Name="NewRemappingBtn" IsEnabled="{x:Bind CanEditMappings, Mode=OneWay}" />
edge_cases: Read-only mode must still allow scrolling and inspecting existing mappings loaded from JSON.
Banner text should cover both missing wrapper DLL and missing Windows App Runtime dependency cases.
Do not expose save-capable controls when native edits cannot be persisted safely.
tests: Add `MainPageFallbackTests` that assert the add button is disabled and the banner is open when startup state is fallback-only.
Manual verification: launch the editor with the native DLL unavailable and confirm the window stays open with a readable error banner.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The constructor creates `KeyboardMappingService` directly, catches any exception, marks `IsServiceRunning = false`, and returns before loading the fallback mappings that `SettingsManager` already prepared.
implementation_steps.change: Use `SettingsManager.StartupState` / `IsNativeServiceAvailable` as the single startup authority. Only create `KeyboardMappingService` when native startup succeeded; otherwise load the JSON-backed collections, set the page into read-only mode, and guard every edit/save/delete entry point against `_mappingService` being null.
edge_cases: Existing methods that call `_mappingService!` must short-circuit in fallback mode instead of null-forgiving into another crash.
`ParseKeyCodes` should keep its current `VK <code>` fallback for missing display-name services.
Periodic service checks must not overwrite the startup-state banner into a misleading “engine down” message.
tests: Add unit tests covering `LoadAllMappings()` with `_mappingService == null` and confirming the existing `EditorSettings` data still populates collections.

Manual repro: rename or remove `PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll` from a debug output folder, launch the editor, and confirm it stays open in read-only mode instead of exiting silently.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The launcher logs only shell-execute failure. If the editor process starts and then dies immediately because of dependency issues, the parent path has no clearer diagnostics than the child log file.
implementation_steps.change: Add launch-side diagnostics for rapid child-process exit and, if needed, a follow-up build assertion in the editor project that verifies the wrapper DLL is present in `WinUI3Apps` before packaging.
edge_cases: Do not block normal startup by waiting too long on the child process.
Keep the hotkey launch path responsive; diagnostics should be lightweight and best-effort.
Avoid false positives when the editor is intentionally reusing an existing process instead of staying in the new one.
tests: Build the Keyboard Manager editor projects and verify `PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll` is present in the `WinUI3Apps` output.
Manual launch from PowerToys should still reuse or open the editor normally when dependencies are healthy.

verify: Build the editor UI project: `pwsh .\tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\src\modules\keyboardmanager\KeyboardManagerEditorUI\KeyboardManagerEditorUI.csproj`

Build the editor UI tests: `pwsh .\tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\src\modules\keyboardmanager\KeyboardManagerEditorUI.UnitTests\KeyboardManagerEditorUI.UnitTests.csproj` and run the focused fallback tests with VS Test Explorer or `vstest.console.exe`.
Confirm the debug `WinUI3Apps` output contains `PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.dll` next to `PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorUI.exe`.
Manual healthy-path check: launch Keyboard Manager editor from PowerToys and confirm it opens and remains editable.

Manual fallback-path check: temporarily rename the wrapper DLL in a debug output copy, launch the editor, and confirm the window stays open in read-only mode with a dependency banner instead of exiting silently.
risks: Opening in read-only fallback mode can confuse users if edit actions still appear enabled, so command gating must be complete.
JSON-only fallback may show raw `VK <code>` names when the native display-name service is unavailable; that is acceptable but should be explained.
Rapid-exit launch diagnostics are heuristic and must not misclassify intentional process reuse as a failure.
alternatives: Showing a message box and exiting would surface the dependency problem, but it would discard the existing JSON-backed fallback the codebase already intends to support.
Removing the standalone fallback entirely would simplify startup but make transient packaging/runtime failures harder for users to diagnose.
Packaging-only fixes help future builds but do not explain or mitigate already-deployed broken installs.
